description: Chlorophytum cremnophilum appears to be an obligatory cremnophyte confined to cliffs of two tributaries of the Gamtoosrivier, the Kougarivier and the Grootrivier. The vegetation consists of Gamtoos Thicket of the Albany Thicket Biome. At the type location and the Grootrivierpoort (Groot Rivier), the plant grows on rock ledges (Cape Supergroup) together with other succulent plants such as Portulacaria afra, Crassula capitella subsp. thyrsiflora, Crassula lactea, C. orbicularis, C. ovata, C. perforata, Crassula pellucida subsp. marginalis, Bulbine natalensis, Bulbine latifolia var. curvata, Haworthia translucens, Ornithogalum longibracteatum, and two species of Delosperma. Along the Kougarivier River (Kougadam) plants were observed growing with Gasteria glomerata, Aloe pictifolia, Cyrtanthus labiatus, C. flammosus and Albuca cremnophila. Plants are locally common and grow in mineral poor quartzitic sandstone cliffs. The climate in its habitat is subtropical with cooler winters but without frost. Temperatures during summers are hot (an average daily maximum of 24-27°C) and the average daily minimum is about 10°C. Rainfall occurs mainly during summer but winter rains are also experienced, ranging from 400-500 mm per annum.

description: The species occurs on steep rocky slopes, along the northern foothills and valleys of the Groot Swartbergerg Mountain in the Western Cape Province of South Africa. It is almost always found on the steep upper portions of north-facing slopes of hills and ridges. It is also found on exposed cliff faces, both in full sun as well as in the shelter of rocks and small karroid shrublets. The habitat of A. tenax is hot and dry, with temperatures up to 30° Celsius in the summer, but as low as 1.7° Celsius during the nights in winter, with light frost, mainly June to August. Mean annual rainfall, for the localities where the plants were observed, ranges from 169-232 mm. This rainfall is spread throughout the year, but in a slight equinoctial pattern, with peaks in autumn (March-April) and spring/early-summer (October-November). Astroloba tenax occurs in the Prince Albert Succulent Karoo (SKvl3) vegetation type, which forms part of Rainshadow Valley Karoo vegetation. In terms of geology, the species favours rocky terrain with limited soils, especially mineral rich shales and tillites. It occurs on rocks of the Karoo Supergroup, specifically the Dwyka and Ecca Groups (Waterford and Fort Brown formations). In the southern part of its range the species occurs on rocks of the Traka Subgroup, of the Bokkeveld Group, of the greater Cape Supergroup.

description: The holotype collection, from 1016 m elevation, occurred on the southern slopes of the Matroosberg Mountain in the FFs8 South Hex Sandstone Fynbos vegetation. The soils are acidic lithosols derived from Ordovician sandstone of the Table Mountain Group. This vegetation is, on the type locality, characterised by sclerophyllous, microphyllous fynbos scrub dominated by proteaceous, ericaceous and asteraceous shrubs, with rich graminoid understory containing numerous Cyperaceae and Restionaceae. The second population was discovered at an elevation of 1920 m, close to the summit of Matroosberg (2249 m). Here Thesium nautimontanum was found in a slight depression supporting a dense restioid-ericoid fynbos wetland (dominated by graminoidsof the family Restionaceae and shrubs of Erica L.), surrounded by dry fynbos scrub of the FFs30 Western Altimontane Sandstone Fynbos. The soils here are nutrient-poor and sandy, overlying Table Mountain Sandstone.

description: It appears to be restricted to patches of quartz-gravel, in Namaqualand Heuweltjieveld and known colloquially as Hardeveld. This is a widespread vegetation type in Namaqualand. The habitat would, however, more correctly be described as an outlier of the Riethuis-Wallekraal Quartz Vygieveld, which occurs only 30 km away, as it is structurally and floristically most similar to this unit. However, units smaller than 1 km in width, as is the case for most quartz patches, are typically unmapped in the South African vegetation map due to scale issues. The underlying rock-type is gneiss, which has weathered into a sandy loam, overlain by large, white quartz-pebbles. Such patches of quartz occupy less than 2% of the total Hardeveld. The slopes may be slightly convex to slightly concave and are north-, west- or south-facing.

description: The underlying rock is Peninsula Formation Quartzitic Sandstone.Aspalathus usnoides is found in Kouga Grassy Sandstone Fynbos (FFs 28).
